note: Canonical web-next performance scenarios + budgets (mirrors config/performance/contract.json culture). Budgets gate local + CI runs of perf/run.mjs against a production build (`next start` on localhost, headless Chromium). Baselines live in BASELINE.md; refresh them before tightening a budget. Pending scenarios are declared here so the runner and budgets exist before their surfaces land — the runner reports them as pending and never fails on them.
ratchet_policy: Budgets are a regression guard against the measured floor, not a target — see docs/perf-floor.md. Two input statistics, depending on what the metric measures: (1) build-artifact-size metrics (first_load_js_kb) are deterministic across runs on a given commit, so budget = ceil(median * 1.10) rounded to the nearest 5kb; (2) wall-clock browser timing metrics (ttft_ms, initial_render_ms, projection_ms, lcp_ms, tbt_ms, resume_ms) are exposed to host CPU scheduling noise, so budget = ceil(max-observed-across-runs * 1.3) rounded to a sensible figure (10-50ms), using at least 10 runs (see BASELINE.md) so the max reflects real tail noise rather than one sample's jitter. Budgets only ever tighten: if the formula's result is above the current budget, the current budget is kept unchanged rather than loosened. #856's refresh ran in a heavily oversubscribed shared sandbox (host load average 35 on 10 cores from concurrent, unrelated CPU-bound agent work) — median*1.25 and even max*1.15 both tripped repeatedly on ordinary noise there (initial_render_ms spanned 79-321ms, resume_ms spanned 143-309ms across 10 otherwise-identical runs). max*1.3 is the margin that held across repeated verification; a quieter CI runner should see it trip only on real regressions.

methodology.paint_timing: waitForFunction polls on requestAnimationFrame, so 'painted' means the frame after the DOM change — within one frame of true paint.
methodology.long_tasks: PerformanceObserver longtask entries, observed in-page. The longtask API only reports tasks >= 50ms, so longest_task_ms reads 0 in a clean run and any nonzero value is a budget violation.
methodology.tbt: Sum of (longtask duration - 50ms) for buffered long tasks within the settle window after navigation.
methodology.first_load_js: Gzipped size of the route's client JS chunks from the .next build manifests — same basis as the `next build` First Load JS column.
methodology.projection: In-process (no browser): perf/projection-bench.mjs, run under tsx, builds a deterministic 200-event log and times projectSessionEvents over N runs after one warmup, printing JSON samples run.mjs aggregates. Measures the pure events→UIMessage[] projection (adapter + readUIMessageStream reduction) that #749's tail/resume path replays through.
methodology.auth: Routes are behind auth (#747). The server runs in test-bypass mode (AUTH_BYPASS=1, throwaway database seeded with one repo + one empty session) and every browser context carries the signed-in test cookie, so route metrics include the middleware + server auth gate — same work production requests do.

scenarios.description: On a real empty session at /sessions/[id], submit a message (the full send path: chat route auth gate, user-event append, mock provider); time from submit to the first assistant token painted in the Folio transcript. One fresh seeded session per run.
While a full mock turn streams into the Folio transcript on /sessions/[id] (prose, ledger rows, diff card, receipt), no main-thread long task may exceed 50ms. One fresh seeded session per run.
Cold production load of /sessions/demo?seed=200 (200 fixture messages, server-rendered); time from navigation start to all 200 messages present in a painted frame.

Project a 200-event session log (20 interleaved user+assistant turns with status/text/tool events) into UIMessage[] in-process; median wall-clock over the runs. This is the read path #749's tail/resume replays; it must stay cheap enough to project a full transcript on reconnect without blocking.
Cold production load of / (the sessions home, one seeded session row, auth gate included): LCP, total blocking time, and first-load JS.
Cold production load of a real empty session at /sessions/[id] (seeded row, Folio surface, autofocused compose): LCP, total blocking time, and first-load JS.
Cold production load of /sessions/demo (Folio session view on fixture data): LCP, total blocking time, and first-load JS.

Load a session whose ~100-event assistant turn was left in flight (seeded stale, no `done`): the client resumes it, the tail route closes the abandoned turn and backfills the whole log. Median time from navigation start to the turn's last event (a marker) painted. One fresh interrupted session per run.
